title: Complete classification of solutions for spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates in R
authors: Xiao Luo, Cunxin Wei, Juncheng Wei, Maoding Zhen
abstract: Spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates provide a fundamental platform for exploring quantum magnetism and coherent spin dynamics. Their three Zeeman components are coupled by spin-exchange interactions under conserved particle number and magnetization, giving rise to rich magnetic phases and nonlinear spin structures; a rigorous classification of stationary states therefore clarifies the possible spin configurations and their physical origins. In this paper, as a continuation of our previous work \cite{LLWZ23,LLWZ24,LLWZ26}, we study the classification of solution for the spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates in $\mathbb{R}$, by applying the non-standard Hirota's bilinear method, the determinant formula and the general left-uniqueness strategy, we present some novel explicit solution and give the complete classification of the solutions. In comparison with the classical Hirota's method, the non-standard Hirota's method needs to introduce auxiliary functions to construct Hirota's bilinear form, which essentially adds additional constraint on the wave functions, so that it possible to deal with more complex equations. As far as we know, this is the first systematic study the complete classification of solutions to the spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates. Our classification results yields experimentally testable predictions for spin populations, relative phases, and magnetic textures
summary: This paper rigorously classifies all stationary solutions for spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates in one dimension. By employing advanced mathematical tools like the non-standard Hirota method, the authors overcome previous limitations to provide a complete catalog of possible spin configurations. The results offer experimentally testable predictions regarding the spin populations and magnetic textures within these quantum magnetic systems.
main_problem: To provide a complete classification of stationary solutions for spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates in one dimension ($\mathbb{R}$).
main_result: The authors present a complete classification of solutions, yielding explicit, novel solutions parameterized by physical constraints like total particle number and magnetization.
method: The classification employs advanced mathematical techniques, including the non-standard Hirota's bilinear method, determinant formulas, and general left-uniqueness strategies.
model_or_system: The system models spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates, governed by a coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equation for three Zeeman components ($\psi_1, \psi_0, \psi_{-1}$), which is a platform for studying quantum magnetism.
key_observables: Spin populations, relative phases, and magnetic textures are predicted by the classification.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($c_0, c_1$), chemical potentials ($\mu, \lambda$), and conserved quantities like total particle number ($N$) and magnetization ($M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the solution belonging to the 'noncollision determinant family' and involves detailed case-by-case analysis based on the support of the asymptotic amplitudes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the stationary equation by applying advanced mathematical methods (non-standard Hirota, determinant formula) to derive constraints on parameters ($\mu, \lambda$) and classify solutions based on the non-zero pattern of asymptotic amplitudes $(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_0, \epsilon_{-1})$.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, complete mathematical classification of the ground and excited states for a fundamental model in ultracold atomic physics, linking abstract mathematical structures to measurable physical quantities.
